import json, glob, os
files = sorted(glob.glob('/root/autodl-tmp/eval_results/*.json')) + sorted(glob.glob('/root/autodl-tmp/eval_results/**/*.json'))
for f in files:
    try:
        d = json.load(open(f))
        name = os.path.basename(f)
        if 'overall' in d:
            tsr = d['overall']['TSR']
            car = d['overall']['CAR']
            total = d['overall']['total_episodes']
            succ = d['overall']['total_success']
            cf = d['overall']['total_collision_free']
            ssr = cf/total if total else 0
            print(f'{name}: TSR={tsr:.3f} CAR={car:.3f} SSR={ssr:.3f} (safe_succ={cf}/{total})')
        elif 'results' in d:
            total_ep = sum(r['n_episodes'] for r in d['results'])
            total_succ = sum(int(r['TSR']*r['n_episodes']) for r in d['results'])
            total_cf = 0
            for r in d['results']:
                for ep in r['episodes']:
                    if ep['success'] and not ep['collided']:
                        total_cf += 1
            tsr = total_succ/total_ep if total_ep else 0
            car_vals = [r['CAR'] for r in d['results']]
            car = sum(car_vals)/len(car_vals)
            ssr = total_cf/total_ep if total_ep else 0
            print(f'{name}: TSR={tsr:.3f} CAR={car:.3f} SSR={ssr:.3f} (safe_succ={total_cf}/{total_ep})')
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'{os.path.basename(f)}: ERROR {e}')
"

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"stdout\": \"\\\\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\\\\label{sec:conclusion}\\n\\nAcross 100+ experiments and 6000+ evaluation episodes on two VLA model families, three findings converge: current VLA safety evaluation is structurally unreliable. Action collapse renders reported CAR illusory (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:dfcar}); EE-only oracle refinement is counterproductive (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:ee_only}); and collision-free demonstrations, not geometric supervision, account for the measured avoidance gains (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:avoidance_source}).\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Why EE-only SDF fails.}\\nTwo independent causes explain the null result. \\\\textit{(i)~Demonstration data subsumes the SDF signal.} Collision-free demonstrations implicitly encode spatial avoidance; the ${\\\\sim}$28\\\\,pp CAR gain arises primarily from this distributional shift, with per-task ordering invariant across all SDF conditions (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:avoidance_source}). At low $\\\\lambda$, SDF is redundant; at $\\\\lambda = 0.1$, the marginal signal preserves the same demonstration-driven pattern. \\\\textit{(ii)~EE monitoring cannot prevent full-body collisions.} The SDF gradient acts on a single point while collisions occur along intermediate links. Oracle experiments confirm this: ground-truth SDF refinement \\\\emph{reduces} CAR by 6--10\\\\,pp below unrefined baselines (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:ee_only}), because pushing the EE away rotates unmonitored links through obstacles. We hypothesize that collision-free demonstration trajectories implicitly encode workspace priors through their spatial distribution: the robot learns to favor regions of the workspace that are inherently collision-free, without requiring explicit geometric supervision. These two causes are independent; effective geometric safety requires both full-body supervision and training signals beyond demonstrations.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Implications for evaluation.}\\ndfCAR corrects action-collapse contamination using only EE position logging, already available in most evaluation pipelines. The bimodal displacement distribution makes $\\\\tau_d$ robust across five orders of magnitude. We recommend reporting both CAR and dfCAR; the gap quantifies contamination. This contamination spans a 4000$\\\\times$ parameter range (Pi0 Full-FT ${\\\\sim}$2.5B to Pi0+A1 ${\\\\sim}$658K trainable), a structural consequence of evaluating avoidance without verifying motion. More broadly, safety may need to operate at the planning or joint-space constraint layer, since any EE-centric loss inherits the same blind spot.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Limitations.}\\nOur evaluation covers one benchmark suite (SafeLIBERO, four tasks) and two model families (Pi0, Pi0.5). The tabletop setting with fixed-base manipulator and known obstacles may not generalize to mobile platforms and cluttered scenes. Oracle experiments used a largely frozen model (Pi0+A1, TSR${\\\\approx}$0\\\\%); testing on an actively moving policy would better isolate the structural limitation. The $\\\\lambda = 0.1$ condition has $n = 2$ seeds; the marginal departure ($p \\\\approx 0.071$, two-tailed permutation test) is inconclusive. Full-body SDF remains untested. Fine-tuning degrades TSR by ${\\\\sim}$21--25\\\\,pp, yet SSR/TSR increases from 0.33 to 0.51--0.57 (Appendix~\\\\ref{sec:appendix_ssr}); reduced exposure alone does not explain the pattern.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Future work.}\\nThree directions follow: (1) full-body SDF supervision along the kinematic chain; (2) cross-architecture evaluation on OpenVLA, RT-2, and other VLA families; (3) planning-layer safety constraints in joint space rather than EE space.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Broader impact.}\\nContaminated CAR scores allow models with no genuine avoidance to pass safety benchmarks. dfCAR exposes this gap with minimal changes to existing protocols.\\n\", \"stderr\": \"\", \"return_code\": 0}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {\"elapsed_seconds\": 0.51}}"}

\section{SDF Ground Truth Pipeline}\label{sec:appendix_sdf_pipeline}

\paragraph{Mesh processing.}
For each SafeLIBERO scene, we extract all visual meshes from the MuJoCo XML model. The \texttt{spatial\_bowl} scene contains 68 meshes (19 initially watertight); \texttt{object\_chocolate} contains 60 meshes (13 initially watertight). We apply automated repair (hole filling, normal correction, winding order fix) via Trimesh, successfully repairing 2/49 and 4/47 non-watertight meshes respectively. Robot arm meshes (complex multi-part geometry) remain non-watertight and are excluded from SDF computation, as the SDF field targets scene obstacles only.

\paragraph{SDF computation.}
Query points are sampled via dual-scale Gaussian ($\sigma_1{=}0.025$, $\sigma_2{=}0.008$, 80\% near-surface) plus 20\% uniform within the bounding box, yielding 4,084 points per scene. SDF values are truncated to $[-0.05, 0.05]$\,m. Key statistics: near-surface ratio ($|$SDF$| < 0.02$) is 61.0--61.5\%; inside ratio (SDF $< 0$) is 20.4--23.8\%.

\paragraph{Gradient verification.}
We verify SDF gradient directions via finite differences ($\epsilon = 10^{-4}$) on 300 near-surface points per scene. Accuracy: 98.7\% (\texttt{spatial\_bowl}), 99.7\% (\texttt{object\_chocolate}). The gradient points away from obstacle surfaces, ensuring that the collision cost $\text{ReLU}(-\text{SDF} + m)$ correctly penalizes proximity.

\paragraph{Sign convention.}
The pysdf library uses positive-inside convention. We apply $\text{SDF} = -\text{pysdf\_output}$ to convert to the standard negative-inside convention. Verified: inside points yield SDF $< 0$ (cost $> 0$); outside points beyond margin yield cost $= 0$.

\section{Evaluation Protocol and Metrics}\label{sec:appendix_eval_protocol}

\paragraph{Task descriptions.}
All four tasks require picking up a target object and placing it in a basket, amid Level-II safety obstacles. The tasks are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item \texttt{chocolate\_pudding}: Pick up chocolate pudding, place in basket.
    \item \texttt{orange\_juice}: Pick up orange juice, place in basket.
    \item \texttt{milk}: Pick up milk, place in basket.
    \item \texttt{bbq\_sauce}: Pick up BBQ sauce, place in basket.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Metrics.}
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{TSR} (Task Success Rate): fraction of episodes where the task is completed.
    \item \textbf{CAR} (Collision Avoidance Rate): fraction of episodes with no collision detected (contact force $>$ 0.001\,m displacement between any robot link and obstacle).
    \item \textbf{dfCAR} (displacement-filtered CAR): CAR computed only over episodes with EE displacement $\geq \tau_d$ (default $\tau_d = 0.1$\,mm).
    \item \textbf{SSR} (Safe Success Rate): fraction of episodes that are both successful and collision-free.
\end{itemize}
